title: plugin-settings@1: the `settings` block of a plugin@1 manifest
description: Brett, Nov 16 2026: "They all need a settings page. They all need a settings interface." Every plugin's settings are one sub-tab of Settings → Plugins (never a top-level tab, never a screen of its own) and every plugin with a screen carries one gear that opens it. Reference engine framework/core/plugin-settings.mjs (defaultSettings, normalizeSettings, checkSettings, settingsAddress); fixture framework/spec/fixtures/plugin-settings.json; check framework/spec/check-plugin-settings.mjs and plugins.mjs --check. A manifest without the block gets the default: its first settings-tab, the three default sections, no options, a gear exactly when it has a screen.

tab.description: Its Settings → Plugins sub-tab: the `settings-tab:<id>` it provides (AxfWebLibrary.settingsTabs[].id). Console-control address view:settings/tab:settings.tabs=plugins/subtab:settings.subtabs=<tab>; runtime action settings.open:<tab>.

parent.description: Always plugins: the console re-parents every plugin tab under Settings → Plugins (App.tsx underPlugins), so a plugin cannot opt out.

sections.description: What the tab shows, in order. Defaults on every plugin: enable (enable / disable), info (name, version, built-with badge, description, dependencies), logs (its log lines). Built-in extras the console draws: options (the keys below), appearance (plugin theme override), placement (Opens in, axf.placement.<id>), commands (plugin-commands@1). A plugin's own panels are sections too, as <plugin>.<section> ids (open registry).

options.description: The real option keys the plugin registers under its tab (SettingSpec.key in its settings groups). Each is reachable as setting:<key> through console control, and read / set the same way through REST, MCP, the CLI and voice. [] = nothing beyond the default sections.

gear.description: A gear on its screen header opens the sub-tab (react/components/PluginSettingsGear, data-axf-target on the button). true whenever the plugin has a screen (a `view:<id>` in provides); false only when it has none. Default: whether it has a screen.
